en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Farmingdale, Monmouth County, New Jersey, October 1923, Sheet 2

sheet-1-1.description: The main map of sheet 1 covers the southern half of the borough of Farmingdale, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 34 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. It runs from Asbury Avenue at the top, where it meets sheet 2, south along Main Street to the borough limits and Public Road, and west across Academy, Walnut and Chestnut Streets to the railroad lines along the western borough limits. Main Street is the commercial spine: stores, a bank, the post office, a moving picture hall, the Presbyterian church, the fire department and the public school stand along it and along Academy, with dwellings behind. Southard Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally; south of it the blocks between Chestnut and Walnut are laid out in narrow lots, mostly still vacant. The Central Railroad of New Jersey crosses the lower half from south-west to north-east, with a freight house beside it, and a second line curves in from the west to join it. Railroad Avenue runs along the north side of the tracks. Industry is grouped near the rails: the A. A. Brant lumber yard, the Folk Printing and Dyeing Corporation cloth printing and dyeing works, the A. C. Soper Company ketchup factory with its elevated water tank, and the Addelson and Sons night-shirt factory south of the tracks, near the depot. Maple Avenue and Boud Avenue carry rows of small dwellings, and the American Hotel and a garage stand south of the tracks on Main Street. The south-east corner is open land beyond the borough limits. The title cartouche, water and fire department notes, a location map of New Jersey and the key are printed on the sheet and are cut out of the mask; an inset in the top left corner is part 2.
notes: Modern names: 2nd St., 3rd St. and 4th St. are 2nd Avenue, 3rd Avenue and 4th Avenue; Public Rd. at the south-west is Marl Road (junction with Central Avenue matched); the Public Rd. east of Main is probably Lakewood Farmingdale Road (not checked).
4th St. and Central meet Railroad Av. about 120 ft apart on the sheet; OpenStreetMap has one node for 4th Avenue, Central Avenue and Railroad Avenue, so that junction was left out.

The sheet fits less well than sheet 2 (RMSE about 5.6 m): Southard Av. and Boud Av. are drawn at angles about 1.7 degrees apart that differ from today's, and the Water St. junctions sit 5 to 10 m off the fit.
Works shown: A. A. Brant Lumber Co., Folk Printing & Dyeing Corp'n, A. C. Soper Co. ketchup factory, Addelson & Sons night-shirt factory.

Scale 100 ft. Title cartouche, water/fire notes, location map and key on the sheet (cut out of the mask). Main map: Main St from Asbury Av south to Public Rd, Academy, Chestnut, Walnut, Water, 2nd-5th Sts, Railroad Av, Maple Av, Boud Av, Central; C.R.R. of N.J. and the Freehold branch. Two parts: 1 main map; 2 inset at top left (Clark Fibre Products Corp'n beside the C.R.R. of N.J., south-west of the main map across match line A-B). North about 34 degrees clockwise from up.

sheet-1-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 1 is an inset in the top left corner of the page, outlined by a heavy line and drawn at the same scale and orientation as the main map (100 feet to an inch, north about 34 degrees clockwise from the top). It continues the main map south-westward along the Central Railroad of New Jersey beyond the match line marked A and B, which is drawn on both parts. The double track runs diagonally across the inset. The only works shown is the Clark Fibre Products Corporation, a single tile building with a concrete floor beside the tracks, with notes that it has no watchman and takes power and light from electricity and heat from steam. Two small buildings sit at the match line at the top right, the same ones drawn at the bottom left corner of the main map. The block number 29 is printed beside the tracks, and a north arrow is drawn in the inset. No street is drawn, so the inset was placed from the buildings and the railroad crossing of the match line that it shares with the main map, at the main map's scale and orientation.
notes: Placed from two points carried from part 1 at the match line A-B (about 50 ft apart), with scale and north taken from the main map; low confidence away from the match line.
Clark Fibre Products Corp'n stands beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey (today's Southern Secondary).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern part of Farmingdale at 100 feet to an inch, with north about 34 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. Main Street runs up the lower part of the sheet from Asbury Avenue to the fork where West Main runs off to the north-west and Murray continues to the north-east; Academy runs parallel to Main on the west, joined to it by Hall. Along Main stand dwellings, the Farmingdale M. E. Church and, behind it, the pump station of the West Monmouth Water Company with its concrete reservoirs. A Roman Catholic church stands in the fork between West Main and Murray. North-east of the fork Murray and Yard Avenue run parallel, crossed by Sheridan, Custer and Kearney; Hancock, at the top, is marked not open. These blocks are laid out in large lots with scattered dwellings and outbuildings, and much of the land, including the large block 24 east of Main and block 15 west of Murray, is open. Water pipes and hydrants are drawn along Main, West Main, Murray and Asbury Avenue. The lower edge repeats the blocks of sheet 1 along Academy and Asbury Avenue. A small cartouche with the town name and date is printed at the top right.
notes: Modern names: Murray is North Main Street; W. Main is West Main Street.
Hancock is marked 'not open' and is not in OpenStreetMap.
Pump station: Fairbanks-Morse and Northern rotary pumps, 10,000 and 60,000 gallon concrete reservoirs.

Scale 100 ft. One part: Main St north of Academy/Hall to W. Main, Murray (now North Main Street), Yard Av, Sheridan, Custer, Kearney, Hancock (not open), Asbury Av at the bottom; pump station. Overlaps sheet 1 along Academy St and Asbury Av. North about 34 degrees clockwise from up.
